summary.en: Law every European Union member state shares: data protection, electronic identification and signatures, the VAT Directive and VAT in the Digital Age, the Eurocodes and the Construction Products Regulation, the procurement directives with TED and eForms, SEPA and instant payments, late payment, the Digital Services Act, the AI Act, the European Accessibility Act and EU financial sanctions. Member packs list this layer and add what is national.

summary.en: Standard and reduced VAT rates are set by each member state: the standard rate is not lower than 15 % (Art. 97 as replaced by Directive (EU) 2018/912); at most two reduced rates not below 5 % for Annex III supplies, plus a limited lower rate or exemption with deduction (Art. 98 as replaced by Directive (EU) 2022/542). Member packs state their rates as tax rate facts.

summary.en: Binding and directly applicable in every member state from 25 May 2018 (Art. 99). Consent must be a freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous statement or clear affirmative action (Art. 4(11)). A personal data breach is notified to the supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours (Art. 33(1)). Data subject requests are answered without undue delay and within one month of receipt, extendable by two further months (Art. 12(3)).

summary.en: Late Payment Directive 2011/7/EU: between undertakings the contractual payment period does not exceed 60 calendar days unless expressly agreed otherwise and not grossly unfair to the creditor (Art. 3(5)); where a public authority pays, 30 calendar days as a rule (Art. 4(3)), with limited extensions up to 60 days. summary.en: Digital Services Act Art. 30: an online platform that lets consumers conclude distance contracts with traders lets a trader offer to consumers in the Union only after obtaining the trader’s name, address, telephone and email, an identification document or eIDAS electronic identification, payment account details, the trade register and number where registered, and a self-certification of compliance with Union law; it makes best efforts to check them against freely accessible official databases (Art. 30(2)), suspends traders who fail to correct inaccurate data (Art. 30(3)) and stores the data for six months after the relationship ends (Art. 30(5)). Not applicable to platforms that are micro or small enterprises (Art. 29).

summary.en: AI Act Art. 50(1): providers design AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons so that those persons are informed they are interacting with an AI system, unless that is obvious to a reasonably well-informed, observant and circumspect person in the context. Applies from 2 August 2026 (Art. 113); Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 kept that date.
